chunks: And from him, from Fadala, from Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked him, 'What about those who seek forgiveness in the early hours of the night?' He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sought forgiveness seventy times in his Witr prayer.'

key_terms.بِالْأَسْحارِ: in the early hours of the night/pre-dawn

ai.seo_question: How many times did the Prophet seek forgiveness in his Witr prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the prophetic practice of intensive repentance during the Witr prayer, a cornerstone of Shia night devotions. By citing the Prophet's recitation of istighfar seventy times, the hadith emphasizes the spiritual discipline of the 'last third of the night' (Qiyam al-Layl), linking personal purification with the culmination of nightly worship. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on following the Ahl al-Bayt's specific liturgical traditions as recorded by scholars like Shaykh al-Tusi.
